1.title: 8강 1번 (50P)
1.q1: 어법상 옳지 않은 선지와, 그 이유는?
1.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
1.passage: Triangle enthusiast Pythagoras thought a lot about music. He studied the lyre, a stringed instrument that was kind of a handheld harp, and developed the mathematics around ① how tone changes with string length. Strike a lyre string and you contribute energy to it, making the string vibrate at a particular frequency that’s a function of its length; your ears experience ② that vibrating energy as a specific tone, like B-flat. Pythagoras believed that everything in the natural world ③ was similarly ruled by math. When he looked up at the night sky, he didn’t just see stars and planets — he saw an elegant equation at work. He believed that each planet emitted a different sound as it rotated and revolved, like the strings of a lyre, each ④ contributes a unique celestial tone to a beautiful cosmic symphony. This concept became ⑤ known as “the music of the spheres.”
1.key_points: 답은 4번이야. 분사구문 contributing을 써야 하는 자리야.

2.title: 8강 2번 (51P)
2.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
2.passage: The growing [[divergence:분기, 갈라짐]] of American communities is important not just in itself but because of what it means for American society. ① While the divide is first and foremost economic, it is now beginning to affect cultural identity, health, family stability, and even politics. ② The sorting of highly educated Americans into some communities and less educated Americans into others tends to [[magnify:확대하다]] and intensify all other socioeconomic differences. ③ For example, there are vast differences in life expectancy among inhabitants of American cities, and these differences have been expanding for the past three decades. ④ Rather than isolating differences, successful societies create space for them to coexist and enrich the broader community. ⑤ The divorce rates, crime rates, and political [[clout:영향력]] of different communities have also been [[diverging:갈라지고 있다]]. These trends are reshaping the very fabric of our society.
2.key_points: 4번이 정답이야. 본문에서 전개하는 '미국 사회의 분열이 초래하는 문제점에 대한 객관적 기술'이 아닌, 이상적 사회에 대한 제언의 개념이므로 서술이 틀려.

3.title: 8강 3번 (52P)
3.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
3.passage:
A few bird species, such as the Woodpecker Finch of the Galápagos Islands, use tools to [[extract:얻어내다]] food. Seventeen species of birds have been shown either in the field or in laboratory studies to craft tools, usually but not always for use in [[foraging:먹이 찾기]].

(A) Knowing the overall details of nest construction is mostly [[innate:타고난]], but assembling nests also requires thought and skill. Birds must find and collect material, which in itself requires some measure of searching and remembering, a form of [[cognitive:인지적인]] behavior.

(B) This, of course, is but a small percentage of the total number of bird species, which is [[approximately:대략, 거의]] 10,000 worldwide. Tool use remains uncommon in birds.

(C) But consider bird nests. The pioneer American [[ornithologist:조류학자]] Alexander Wilson described in detail how a female Orchard Oriole [[intricately:복잡하게]] weaves grasses to form the hanging nest. Constructing an oriole nest would be [[challenging:어려운, 도전적인]] for any human.
3.key_points: 올바른 순서는 B C A 야.

4.title: 8강 4번 (53P)
4.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
4.passage:
Children come by their excitement naturally. Until it gets crushed out of them in school, kids
innately know how to have fun and love what they do.

(A) But as Csikszentmihalyi noted, “Most enjoyable activities are not natural; they demand an effort
that initially one is reluctant to make.” Some activities will only engross us if we take the
trouble to pay close attention to them.

(B) Simply put, flow is when your concentration is such that you lose all sense of time and place.
The experience is its own reward; its end goal or outcome is just the icing on the cake. The
satisfactions that go with creating an inspired work of art or flawlessly executing an athletic feat
are easy enough to imagine.

(C) Give them a wooden stick and watch as they begin to play with it. Wait a while and ask them
what it is. You will get answers like “It’s a car!” or “It’s a rocket!” Kids have an
unlimited capacity not just for fantasy and imagination but for engrossment, much as artists or
athletes do when they are experiencing the mental state that my mentor Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
famously described as “flow.”
4.key_points: 이 글의 답은 C B A 순서야.

5.title: 8강 5번&6번 (54P)
5.passage:
Parents as gardeners and children as flowers have been popular and fitting parenting analogies for
the years between birth and twelve. However, seeing our adolescent children as flowers somehow
does not ring true. Their growth and development have a (a) different quality than the flowering
plants of childhood. Eugene Schwartz writes of teenagers, “And what of the abnormal, poisonous
plant? Here we see a picture of adolescence!” Like weeds, our teens go through a period of
growing (b) inward, turning away from the light, seeking to create a space within themselves that
clearly says, “This is me!” Like weeds, young teenagers create a private, inner pocket; they turn
back upon themselves, (c) revisiting what they had previously rejoiced in, withdrawing from the
forces of nature that had previously nurtured them. The dilemma for the parent as gardener
becomes a process of learning how to care for a weed, when all the experiences we have ever had
with weeds (d) push us to spray them dead, dig them out, and throw them away. Many of us gain a
therapeutic satisfaction from digging weeds in our gardens, ridding our flower beds of that gangly
plant that (e) refuses to grow like the other flowers; its leaves a little too sharp, its stem a bit too
woody, its essence too poisonous. Some days we all feel the urge to pull out the teenage weed by
the roots and throw it out the window! But the feeding and caring of a teenage weed is a much
more delicate bit of gardening. We are responsible for its care, its well-being, and its development.
5.key_points: 문맥상 옳지 않은 낱말을 찾는 문제고, 정답은 (c) 야.

6.title: 10강 1번 (62P)
6.q1: 문맥상 옳지 않은 선지는? 그리고 그것이 문맥상 옳지 않은 이유는?
6.q2: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
6.passage: Awards can strengthen people’s [[commitment:헌신, 전념]] to the organization giving the award. The [[intrinsic:내재적인]] motivation to perform well and in the interest of the employer is ① praised by the giver and hence reinforced. In contrast, when an attempt is made to measure performance by pay, this intrinsic work motivation may well be [[crowded out:밀려나다/배제되다]]. After all, performance pay may unintentionally ② signal that the ultimate goal of all [[endeavours:노력]] is to get money. All that matters is to reach the [[criteria:기준]] in order to get the bonus promised. The content of work becomes ③ [[secondary:부차적인]]. Employees [[are induced:유도되다]] to disregard everything not covered by the criteria imposed even if they know this is — ④ [[detrimental:해로운]] for the organization they work for. Moreover, employees promised bonuses have a strong [[incentive:장려책, 원동력]] to exploit the system. If shareholder value is used as the major criterion for CEOs, they may artificially increase this number by short-term [[manipulations:조작, 조종]] or by buying back shares. The resulting shareholder value then does not reflect the [[underlying:근본적인]] state of the corporation but may be ⑤ biased in favour of short-run effects.
6.key_points: 정답 선지는 3번이야. 앞 맥락에서 '돈을 얻고자 하는 목표가 가장 중요해진다'라는 내용이 등장하므로, 업무의 내용은 부수적인 것이 된다고 표현하는 것이 옳아.

7.title: 10강 2번 (63P)

7.passage:

 Faces cannot be [[discounted:무시되다]] as carriers of emotion. 8.title: 10강 3번 (64P)
8.q1: 주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치와, 그 이유는?
8.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
8.passage:
The prevailing explanation of human action was that people were “pushed” by their internal drives or “pulled” by external events.

The science of psychology has not always cared about individual styles of thinking, or about individual human action or the individual at all. Quite the opposite. When I was a graduate student in psychology, twenty-five years ago, psychological dilemmas involving individual choice were not explained the way they are today. ( ① ) At that time, people were assumed to be products of their environment. ( ② ) Though the details of the pushing and pulling depended on the particular theory you happened to hold, in outline all the fashionable theories agreed on this proposition. ( ③ ) The Freudians held that unresolved childhood conflicts drove adult behavior. ( ④ ) The followers of B. F. Skinner held that behavior was repeated only when reinforced externally. ( ⑤ ) The ethologists held that behavior resulted from fixed action patterns determined by our genes, and the behaviorist followers of Clark Hull held that we were goaded into action by the need to reduce drives and satisfy biological needs.

9.title: 10강 4번 (65P)
9.q2: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
9.q3: 이 글에 의하면, 유년기와 성인기에 대한 청소년의 차이는 무엇인가?
9.passage:
Adults make their own decisions, and children have most of their decisions made for them.
Teenagers, of course, are stuck somewhere in the middle. As they gradually gain more freedom, they
must learn to plan what to do with that freedom. To equip them for this, they are poised at the
most exciting point in the story of human cerebral change — the human brain changes throughout life, but that change is most complex in the second decade. Recent scientific discoveries go a long
way towards showing that adolescence is, perhaps surprisingly, the high point of the human brain — when the brain is at its largest, most flexible, and most changeable. The teenage years are when our
greatest asset — our mind — is most strongly shaped. Change in the teenage body is important, but
for humans, change in the brain is more important still.

11.title: Mini Test 2 2번 (109P)
11.q2: 글에 드러난, 변하기 전 심경을 드러내는 표현은?
11.q3: 글에 드러난, 변한 뒤의 심경을 드러내는 표현은?
11.passage:
Our group had just finished performing our routine for the competition to join the Richfield
Cheerleading Team and was waiting offstage. The coach told us that the judges would be tabulating
scores. Meanwhile, I sat with my friends and tried to act normal. Inside, however, I could feel the
butterflies not only fluttering wildly in my stomach, but also flapping their wings so strongly that I
actually felt sick. Holding hands, we lowered our heads and waited for the decision. Finally, the
numbers of the lucky girls were announced. I did not register any of the numbers until I heard the
coach say, “ …One.” I looked down at my sticker to make sure that the number one was written on it. I had finally made the team! My dream had become reality!
